item.title: Kabira Bay — Guide
item.description: Kabira Bay (Kabira-wan), on Ishigaki Island in the Yaeyama group, is one of the most beautiful and famous scenic views in all of Okinawa, and a designated national scenic spot. The bay is a stunning composition of shifting emerald and turquoise water, brilliant white sand and small forest-covered islets, its colours changing with the light and tide throughout the day. Because of strong currents, swimming is not permitted in the bay, but the star way to experience it is by glass-bottom boat, which glides over vibrant coral gardens and tropical fish — a great option for families and non-divers.

item.title: Yaeyama Islands Guide: Ishigaki, Iriomote & Taketomi
item.description: Japan’s southwesternmost frontier, the Yaeyama Islands are a tropical archipelago of jungle, coral and old Ryukyu charm — closer to Taiwan than to Tokyo. Gateway island Ishigaki dazzles with the emerald Kabira Bay, while neighbouring Iriomote is a wild, mangrove-and-jungle island roamed by the rare Iriomote cat, and tiny Taketomi preserves a postcard village of red-tiled houses and water-buffalo carts. Linked by quick ferries, the Yaeyama are an island-hopper’s dream.
